answer.rationale: Competitor's price cut creates immediate churn risk in price-sensitive SMB segment. Memory_73 confirms targeted promotional pricing is effective for SMB acquisition and revenue lift in exactly this scenario. A standard-experiment rollout of time-limited promotional pricing on SMB accounts at churn risk preserves the option to layer onboarding simplification (memory_31) and activation messaging (memory_91) once pricing stabilizes. This avoids competitive capitulation while maintaining focus on qualified revenue. Enterprise segment should remain protected via sales-assisted flows (memory_44) without promotional dilution. Referral incentives (memory_57) are better deployed post-stabilization to established customer base, not during acute churn crisis. Risk: extended price discounting can erode margin and anchor customer price expectations; mitigation requires strict time-bounding and clear expiration. Uncertainty preserved: churn elasticity at this depth and velocity is untested; standard experiment allows measurement before broad commitment.
